headline: High: shared filesystem, broad egress, and overlapping write/tooling make prompt injection, leakage, and conflict plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; nullclaw reads/writes workspace files and exposes webhooks, ws, and agent-card surfaces. A shared local filesystem or copied content can carry attacker-controlled instructions between them, so injection is plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory or copied file contents
IF nullclaw webhook or ws payloads are forwarded into Cursor buffers or MCP inputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable clipboard bridging between agents
Treat all file and webhook content as untrusted
Require explicit human review before acting on imported instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor has broad network egress and handles open files plus optional API keys; nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files. If they share files or memory, sensitive material can flow into Cursor and then out through model-provider or API calls, creating an exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF either agent opens the other's workspace files containing secrets
IF Cursor sends those contents to model providers or api.cursor.sh
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Store credentials in separate vaults per agent
Disable automatic file-context upload for sensitive directories
Rotate any exposed keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write files, modify git state, install packages, and use MCP. Cursor explicitly shares state via the local filesystem, while nullclaw uses a durable memory namespace and workspace files. Concurrent writes to the same repo or config can race and corrupt state without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or config directory
IF either agent runs git or package-install actions without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches
Serialize git and package operations
Use file locks around shared mutable paths
Run one agent at a time for write-heavy tasks
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can act as an autonomous coding agent with shell and MCP tools, and nullclaw can ingest webhooks, agent-card data, and conversation history. If one agent's output is treated as authoritative by the other, errors can cascade into code changes, API actions, or scheduled tasks without a verification step.
conditions: IF Cursor-generated code or instructions are fed into nullclaw automation
IF nullclaw webhook or agent-card content is consumed by Cursor without validation
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Add schema validation to all inter-agent messages
Compare outputs against independent sources
Limit automation to read-only dry runs
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is closed-source and routes data to model providers, while nullclaw is documented as touching API keys, bearer tokens, private keys, and webhook payloads. If regulated or secret-bearing data is shared across the pair, residency and retention obligations can be breached; the profiles do not show a shared compliance boundary.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or personal data are placed in shared workspaces
IF either agent forwards that data to external APIs or logs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings
Disable logging for sensitive sessions
Use separate tenants or regions where available
requires-engineering: formalize data-class routing and residency controls
